images.title: Large numbers in a box of stickers
images.purpose: Show how a large count is found: count one small part, multiply by the number of parts, and then count the digits.
images.composition: From left to right: one sticker sheet, a box of 40 sheets, and the product written large on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas, three parts from left to right. LEFT: one square sticker sheet with a thin dark outline, holding exactly 10 rows of 10 small round stickers, 100 stickers in all, all in teal #0072B2. Under the sheet the text 1 sheet, and under that the text 100 stickers. MIDDLE: an open flat box seen from the side, holding a thick stack of sheets drawn as one slab (individual sheets are not drawn), amber #E69F00 box. A plain thick arrow points from the sheet to the box. Under the box the text 40 sheets. RIGHT: in very large type the equation 100 × 40 = 4,000, and under it the text 4-digit number with a thin bracket under the number 4,000. Nothing else is drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Count one part, multiply by the number of parts, and the digits tell if the count is a 4-digit or a 5-digit number.
images.description: One sheet of 100 stickers and a box of 40 sheets make 100 × 40 = 4,000 stickers, a 4-digit number.
images.context: The chapter's own idea is a book with pages and words grouped into a large count. The plan uses its own numbers from the concept's worked example, stickers, so that the printed example of the book stays a question for the student. The 10 by 10 grid shows what 100 looks like.
images.teaching_notes: Say: one sheet has 100, ten sheets have 1,000, forty sheets have 4,000. Then count the digits of 4,000. Do not use the numbers of pages and words of the book's printed example here.

image_decisions.why: A drawn sheet and box make the idea of counting one part and multiplying to reach a large count concrete.
